intent.quote: It shouldn't just one question if there are more questions. Question tool should be more practical than cards to clarify the intent I think. Clarify should ask specific questions that clarify the intent to make the intent clear for the next steps.
intent.readback: When you want intent clarified you say so with /plumb intent and your words, and plumb works like a brainstorming partner: it reads your words with the conversation, assumes what it can recommend, and asks every question that changes what gets built, specific and all at once, through the question tool. Outside that loop plumb only stops edits when a request would contradict or extend what you already confirmed. Big work is handled as one set, repaired by the agent and approved in one step by the judge.
will: Open one intent loop on /plumb intent with your words; an ordinary message opens none.
Ask every blocking question, specific, with options and a recommendation, through the question tool (or the browser study room when a trade-off needs study), scaled to the request.
Turn a gap with a better-supported option into a labelled, flippable assumption instead of a question.
Run each stage of the loop only on the passed gate of the stage before, the judge gate being the judge cascade.
Close the edit gate outside the loop only when a request or edit would contradict or extend a confirmed record, and put that contradiction to you as one question.
Handle a big request as one set the agent repairs until clean and the judge approves in one step.
wont: Analyse every message with a model: outside the loop only messages touching a confirmed record are judged.
Close the edit gate on a question, a notice or a change no confirmed record covers.
Show you a read-back or a card to read and press, or ask you to approve a set by command or id.
Ask what the records, the code, the conversation or a sensible default already answer.
assumptions: The loop's judge gate is P9's cascade: JEV above 0.9 fast-tracks, else Sonnet asks through the question tool, then JEV again.
Opening the gate means answering the question it raised; there is no release command.
The big-request thresholds (3 requirements, 1 feature, 400 lines, 10 files) carry over unchanged from the confirmed SR-036.
A loop or gate that cannot settle goes to P5's debug workflow; the owner is asked only as a last resort.
Each proof plan is the AI's recommendation; the owner decides the proof (P10).

requirements.title: /plumb intent opens one intent loop whose stages each run only on the previous stage's passed gate
requirements.statement: Typing /plumb intent with the owner's words opens one loop for that intent: the clarifier asks its blocking questions through the question tool, checks each answer against the confirmed records, writes the intent candidates and passes them through one judge gate, the judge cascade as P9 defines it, fixing until only low findings remain. Each later stage (update records and plans, build, then the proof P10 requires) refuses to run until the previous stage's gate passed; a gate that cannot settle goes to P5's debug workflow. An ordinary message opens no loop.

examples.when: the owner types /plumb intent add multiply next to add
examples.then: the blocking questions come through the question tool, as many as there are gaps, and no record is written until the intent is clear

examples.given: an intent candidate contradicts a confirmed requirement's example
examples.then: the contradiction is put to the owner as one question through the question tool before the candidate is written, in plain words and without a record id

examples.given: the judge gate finds a high finding on a candidate
examples.then: the candidate is fixed and judged again, and the loop ends only when every finding left is low

examples.then: it refuses and names the gate that has not passed

examples.given: the judge gate passed with only low findings
examples.then: it proceeds and records that it ran on that gate

examples.given: the build stage finished
examples.when: the proof the owner chose has not been shown
examples.then: the loop does not close: its last stage names the proof gate (P10) as not passed

requirements.title: The clarifier reads the owner's words in context and asks every blocking question, specific, through the question tool
requirements.statement: Inside the loop the clarifier reads the owner's words with the agent's last reply, the owner's recent messages and repository facts, and acts only on a change to the system being built. A gap with a better-supported option becomes a labelled, flippable assumption; every gap whose answer changes what gets built is asked in the same turn, specific, with options and a recommendation, through the question tool. The owner never reads the interpretation itself. The owner's answers are logged as their words and never asked again; nothing of the clarifier's self-questioning is recorded.

examples.when: the owner says 'resolve all of the findings using a workflow'
examples.then: no question asks which findings: the interpretation assumes the findings listed above and the work goes on

examples.given: the agent diagnosed why the panel does not show

requirements.title: The clarifier's false-gap rate is measured on an evaluation set before calibration
requirements.statement: Before calibration, the clarifier runs on an evaluation set of requests that need no clarification and requests with known gaps; its false-gap rate (questions that change nothing about what gets built) is measured and reported with the calibration results.

examples.given: an evaluation set holding requests that need no clarification and requests with known gaps
examples.when: the clarifier is run on it before calibration
examples.then: its false-gap rate (questions that change nothing about what gets built) is measured and reported with the calibration results

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: the owner asks plumb how well the clarifier does and is shown its false-gap rate on the evaluation set beside the calibration results.

requirements.title: Outside the loop the edit gate closes only when a request or edit would contradict or extend a confirmed record
requirements.statement: Outside the intent loop the edit gate closes only when the configured judge finds that a request or an edit contradicts or extends a confirmed record's examples and no loop has run for it; it opens when a loop reaches clear intent for it or the owner answers the question it raised. A question, a notice or a change no confirmed record covers never closes it. The gate belongs to one session and one owner message.

examples.when: the prompt says make add subtract
examples.then: the judge flags a contradiction naming that example, the edit gate closes, and the contradiction is put to the owner as one question through the question tool

requirements.title: The edit gate cannot be switched off by accident
requirements.statement: The edit gate is enforced wherever the session runs: a settings file that allows plumb's hook command without running it, or a session started in a subfolder of an adopted repository, still has edits refused while the gate is closed; plumb's plugin hooks stand down only for a legacy install that already runs plumb's hooks, so nothing runs twice.

examples.when: an edit tool is called while the gate is closed
examples.then: the edit is refused

examples.given: Claude Code started in src/ of an adopted repository
examples.when: an edit tool is called while the gate is closed
examples.then: the edit is refused

examples.given: a legacy install whose hook commands run plumb hook
examples.then: the plugin's hook does nothing, so nothing runs twice

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: with the gate closed in a scratch repository, the owner starts Claude Code in its src/ folder and sees the agent's edit refused.

requirements.title: A big request's records are approved as one set, in one step
requirements.statement: In the loop a big request's records are one set; once clean, the judge cascade approves it in one step under one set hash over its members' hashes, marked judge-approved; editing a member unconfirms it and the set. With no judge reachable the set is held, never approved by rule.

examples.given: an intent with members SR-070 and SR-071, clean
examples.when: the judge cascade validates the set
examples.then: one approval event, marked judge-approved, carries the set hash of the sorted [id, hash] pairs and approves all three records

examples.given: the set is approved
examples.then: SR-071 is an unconfirmed edit and the set shows as unconfirmed

examples.given: a clean set and no judge reachable
examples.then: plumb says so and holds the set; nothing is approved by rule

requirements.title: A big request gets the intent loop suggested once, in one line
requirements.statement: plumb suggests the intent loop once, in one line and never as a question, for a big request: more than 3 requirements, more than one feature, a contradicted confirmed record, shared surfaces, hard-to-undo effects, two open decisions that matter, or a diff past 400 lines or 10 files. A declined suggestion is not repeated for that intent.

examples.given: a prompt matching records of FEAT-001 and FEAT-003
examples.then: it suggests the intent loop in one line with the reason "touches 2 features", never as a question

examples.given: a turn whose diff has 450 changed lines and no approved set
examples.then: the agent is told in one line that the intent loop is suggested, with the reason 'diff past 400 lines'

examples.given: the owner declined the suggestion for an intent
examples.when: the same trigger fires again for that intent
examples.then: no suggestion is shown and an escalation-declined event exists

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: in a live session the owner asks for a change touching two features and sees the one-line suggestion once; declining it, the owner does not see it again for that intent.

requirements.title: A big request's set is repaired by the agent until it is clean
requirements.statement: plumb checks a big request's set for structural gaps (a requirement with no example, a will against a won't) and hands each fixable gap to the agent, never to the owner, until the check is clean; a set that is not clean cannot be approved. A trade-off between the owner's own lines is the one thing asked, as one question that becomes a decision that matters.

examples.given: a big set where one requirement has no example
examples.then: the gap goes to the agent, the agent adds the example, and the next check is clean

examples.given: a set whose will "email the reminders" goes against its won't "keep email addresses"
examples.then: the owner is asked one question about that trade-off through the question tool, recorded as a decision that matters

examples.given: a set that is not clean
examples.when: approval of the set is sought
examples.then: it is refused, naming the gaps to the agent

examples.given: any gap the agent can fix
examples.then: the owner never sees it

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: in a live session a big request whose set lacks an example is repaired by the agent with nothing shown to the owner, and a will against a won't reaches the owner as one question.

decisions.question: Does the intent loop run on every request, or on command, and what opens it?
decisions.chosen: On command: /plumb intent with the owner's words opens the loop; ordinary work keeps the background grounding, where a model judges a message only when it touches a confirmed record.
alternatives: Always orchestrated: every request goes through the stages.
Grounding only: no stages, the loop becomes guidance for agents.
Open it with /plumb design, /plumb shape, or a widened /plumb clarify.

decisions.question: Do clarification and integration against the records run as one loop or two?
decisions.chosen: One loop with one judge gate: checking each answer against the records is what makes the questions fewer.
alternatives: Two stages, each with its own judge gate.

decisions.question: How is each stage's review step enforced?
decisions.chosen: By the stage commands: the next stage refuses to run without the previous stage's passed gate, recorded in the intent's session state and carried as workflow phases; hooks only close the edit gate on an intent change and hold the merge.
alternatives: Every stage gate as a hook.

decisions.question: How are the clarifier's gaps handled?
decisions.chosen: A gap with a recommendable option becomes a flippable assumption; every other gap that changes what gets built is asked, all of them, specific, through the question tool.
alternatives: At most one card per turn.
One card with up to three questions.

retired_decisions.why: it sizes a one-line offer the owner confirms with 'ok' and the agent relays (plumb relay --group); the owner approves nothing by reading, the judge cascade approves a set in one step (P2, P3, P9)
